rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the latest first working day: if it is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03. → 01.04.). It is always derived again when the first working day changes.

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, Married and Registered partnership count as 'Married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'Not married'.

rules.statement: An employee who is married or in a registered partnership is exempt from source tax if the spouse/partner lives in Switzerland and is Swiss or holds a C permit.

rules.statement: The digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose result is 'Counted' or 'Counted with H'; 0 without children. (The formal expression covers one child block; the digit is the sum over all children.)

rules.statement: For employees living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies if they return daily and have provided a certificate of residence, or if they do not return daily, a daily return is reasonable and they do not expect more than 60 non-return days. 'Not yet' for the certificate counts as no. In all other cases the normal tariff applies.

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: Base letter: C or B for married employees/registered partners (spouse employed or not); H for non-married employees with an H child; otherwise A. If the cross-border tariff applies, the letter is mapped A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P.

rules.name: Source tax result
rules.statement: Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code for every employee subject to source tax: tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y, H2N). For Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days the result is 'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. Employees not subject get no result. The result is always derived again from the latest answers.

table.then: Not subject to source tax (no tariff code)
In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement (flagged for HR)
Tariff code = tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix

rules.expression: if_else(subject_to_source_tax, if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, "In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", "Tariff code"), "Not subject to source tax")

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder, so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: If the employee changes an earlier answer so that later questions no longer apply, those answers may be kept while the employee goes back and forth, but are discarded on submission. After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee; later changes are made by HR.

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee of Muster AG answers one short questionnaire in Lonio. It asks each piece of information once, and only when a receiving party needs it for this person. From the answers Lonio records everything the pension fund registration, the source tax tariff code and HR need, without further questions.
feature.context:
Today HR at Muster AG (the customer company) collects the onboarding data from each new employee. HR posts many documents to employees, so a complete postal address matters (F-hr_transcript-5518ad, F-hr_transcript-66fe15). The first working day often moves, for example after an earlier exit is agreed with the old employer. The pension fund insurance start date depends on it (F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-1d5c07). Pensionskasse Muster rejects a registration with missing required fields, such as the spouse's date of birth for married employees (F-pension_portal-ef28c3). To find the source tax tariff, HR clicks through the Canton of Zurich calculator (F-hr_transcript-4e180e). Lonio will compute the full tariff code itself (D-001).

Lonio must ask every question at most once and reuse the answer for every receiving party. Asking too little blocks a registration. Asking too much collects personal data no party may have (G-01, data minimisation). Wherever possible Lonio asks for primary facts and derives values from them (G-08).

Questionnaire flow overview:
1. Personal details: first name, last name, date of birth. Always asked.
2. Home address: street, house number, postcode, town, country. Then the canton, only for employees living in Switzerland (D-002).
3. Start of employment: the first working day. The insurance start date is derived from it.
4. Nationality and permit: only for employees living in Switzerland. They give their nationality; non-Swiss employees also say whether they hold a C permit (D-005, D-008).
5. Civil status and spouse: civil status is always asked. The spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked of married, registered and separated employees (D-003, D-004). The spouse's country of residence, nationality and C permit are asked only when they can decide source tax liability.
6. Source tax: only for employees subject to source tax. Denomination, whether the spouse or partner is employed, and whether the employee has children.
7. Children: one block per child, following the calculator's child logic.
8. Cross-border commuting: only for employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein (D-007, D-035).
9. Finish: a permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad (D-010, D-038), then submission. After submission the questionnaire is read-only (D-036, D-037).

Only the employee side is in scope. Out of scope are:
- transmission of data to the receiving parties (G-04)
- AHV data and IT equipment (G-03)
- HR screens and any HR changes after submission (D-034).

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and full postal address, plus the canton for residents of Switzerland. The pension fund needs these to register the employee, HR needs them to post documents, and the address country decides most later conditions.

stories.title: Personal details for the pension fund registration
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered as an insured person. The registration is rejected when any of these required fields is empty.
stories.priority_reason: All three are required fields of the pension fund registration. Pensionskasse Muster rejects a registration with missing required fields, which blocks the process.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the first step, 'Personal details'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name, last name and date of birth, whatever their other answers. They cannot submit the questionnaire while any of the three is empty.

examples.name: Any employee, regardless of later answers

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is a calendar date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter it
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is a full calendar date, shown and recorded as DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.02.1990), as the pension fund registers it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are recorded once for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the pension fund registration is prepared
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name and date of birth are recorded for the pension fund registration as the employee entered them. No later step asks for them again.

stories.title: Complete home address for posting documents
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their full home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee, using the address as one would write it on an envelope
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states that the address has to be complete. An incomplete address stops documents from reaching the employee.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five address parts are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is in the 'Home address' step of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country. All five are required for every employee, wherever they live, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while any part is empty.

acceptance_criteria.title: A normal postal address, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the address step is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: only the parts of a normal postal address are asked (street, house number, postcode, town, country), as written on an envelope. The country is given by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany", "Liechtenstein".

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: HR needs to post a document to the employee
acceptance_criteria.then: the complete home address is recorded for HR as the employee entered it.

stories.title: Home address country is the country of residence for later questions
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to count as the employee's country of residence for all later questions
stories.so_that: whether the employee lives abroad (and so is subject to source tax), and in which state of residence, is known without asking again
stories.priority_reason: Living abroad decides source tax liability and the cross-border part of the tariff code. Asking it twice would contradict the ask-once principle.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is never asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: later steps need to know where the employee lives (main residence in Switzerland or not, state of residence)
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio takes the home address country as the country of residence. The employee is not asked about residence again.

acceptance_criteria.title: State of residence for source tax follows the address country
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the state of residence for source tax is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: Switzerland gives 'Switzerland', Germany gives 'Germany', Liechtenstein gives 'Liechtenstein', and any other country gives 'Other country'. The cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein are specified in the cross-border section.

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax without a nationality question
acceptance_criteria.given: the home address country is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides which questions follow
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee counts as subject to source tax whatever their nationality, and is not asked for nationality, C permit or canton. An employee living in Switzerland is asked for their nationality and canton.

sections.title: Source tax liability check
sections.purpose: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax with as few questions as possible: home country, then nationality and C permit for residents of Switzerland, then the spouse's residence, nationality and C permit. Only employees subject to source tax get the tariff questions.

stories.title: Ask Swiss citizenship and C permit only of employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: to give my nationality, and whether I hold a C permit, only when I live in Switzerland and it matters for my source tax liability
stories.so_that: Lonio can tell whether I am subject to source tax without collecting personal data that no receiving party needs
stories.priority_reason: Without nationality and C permit Lonio cannot decide source tax liability for residents of Switzerland. HR today does not know up front who has to answer the source tax questions. Data minimisation (G-01) makes asking too much a compliance issue.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality is asked only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the nationality and permit step
acceptance_criteria.then: the nationality is asked, and must be answered, only if the home address country is Switzerland. Employees living abroad are not asked for their nationality, because they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality. The nationality is recorded for source tax and for HR, which uses it for the permit reminder to non-Swiss employees.

examples.name: Swiss citizen living abroad, like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-1a20bb)

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality is given as a country; Swiss citizens answer Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and is asked for their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the nationality is given as a country by its English name (e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany"). Anyone holding Swiss citizenship answers "Switzerland", even if they also hold another nationality, and counts as Swiss for source tax. Whether to ask only 'Swiss citizen yes/no' instead is open (see OQ-nationality-wording).

acceptance_criteria.title: C permit is asked only of non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and has given their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: the nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they hold a C permit (permanent residence), answered with "yes" or "no", and must answer it. The answer is recorded for source tax. Swiss employees and employees living abroad are not asked.

examples.name: Swiss citizen (also dual citizen) living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: The permit type itself is never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the permit question
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio only asks whether they hold a C permit. It does not ask which other permit they hold (e.g. B permit), because no receiving party needs it.

stories.title: Ask spouse details only when the spouse could exempt the employee
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask about the spouse or registered partner (where they live, their nationality, their C permit) only when that can exempt the employee from source tax
stories.so_that: employees like Tomás, married to a Swiss wife living in Switzerland, are correctly found not subject to source tax, without asking every married employee about their spouse
stories.priority_reason: The spouse exemption decides source tax liability. A wrong decision gives a wrong tariff or asks source tax questions of people who do not need them. Data minimisation (G-01) limits the spouse questions to the cases where they decide something.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's country of residence is asked first, and only when it can matter
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has answered "no" to holding a C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked in which country their spouse or registered partner lives, given as a country by its English name, and must answer it. It is recorded for source tax. It is not asked of single, divorced, widowed or separated employees, because separated counts as single for source tax. It is also not asked of employees who are Swiss, hold a C permit or live abroad, because the spouse cannot change their liability. Asking the residence before nationality and permit is inferred from data minimisation: a spouse living outside Switzerland never exempts.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality is asked only if the spouse lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has been asked where their spouse or registered partner lives
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for the spouse's nationality, given as a country by its English name, and must answer it. A spouse holding Swiss citizenship is entered as "Switzerland", even with another nationality. Applying the dual-citizenship rule to the spouse is an inference (see OQ-nationality-wording). It is recorded for source tax. If the spouse lives in any other country, neither the spouse's nationality nor their C permit is asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's C permit is asked only for a non-Swiss spouse living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse or registered partner lives in Switzerland and the employee has given the spouse's nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse's nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether the spouse holds a C permit, answered with "yes" or "no", and must answer it. It is recorded for source tax. It is not asked for a Swiss spouse, and the spouse's other permit types are never asked.

acceptance_criteria.then: the state of residence is Switzerland when the country is Switzerland, Germany when it is Germany, Liechtenstein when it is Liechtenstein, and 'other country' for any other country. stories.title: Decide the cross-border tariff for employees living in Germany

stories.so_that: Lonio applies the cross-border tariff (letters L, M, N, P) or the normal tariff exactly as the Zurich calculator does
stories.priority_reason: HR finds the questions for employees living abroad the hardest part of the calculator (F-hr_transcript-ab8886). Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001), so a wrong cross-border decision gives a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return is asked only of employees living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address country is Germany, so they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the 'Cross-border commuting' step, after the children
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany (yes or no). Employees living anywhere else are not asked. The answer is recorded for the source tax tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only of daily returners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany has said they return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say whether they have provided a certificate of residence: yes, no or not yet. 'Not yet' is a valid answer. No document is uploaded in Lonio; the certificate goes to HR outside Lonio. The answer is recorded for the tariff code and for HR, so HR knows when a certificate is still outstanding. Employees who do not return daily are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Reasonable daily return and non-return days are asked only when they decide the tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany has said they do not return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say whether a daily return would in principle be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance), yes or no. Only if it is reasonable must they also say whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, yes or no. This is a declaration of what they expect for the year; no proof is asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff or normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered the cross-border questions that apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border tariff applies only to employees living in Germany who either return daily and have provided a certificate of residence, or do not return daily, for whom a daily return is reasonable and who do not expect more than 60 non-return days. 'Not yet' for the certificate counts as 'no'. In every other case the normal tariff applies. When the cross-border tariff applies, the tariff letter becomes L instead of A, M instead of B, N instead of C and P instead of H (e.g. L0Y, N1Y). Child digit and church-tax suffix do not change.

flow.intro: The questionnaire has nine steps. Only the questions that apply to the employee are shown, and a step with no applicable question is skipped. Employees living abroad skip step 4. Employees not subject to source tax skip steps 6, 7 and 8. Employees without children skip step 7. Everyone except residents of Germany or Liechtenstein skips step 8. The order follows what each answer depends on. The home address country (step 2) decides who gets the nationality and permit questions (step 4). Nationality, permit and the family details (steps 4 and 5) decide whether the employee is subject to source tax. Only then come the source tax questions: general details (step 6), one block per child (step 7) and cross-border commuting (step 8), in the same order as the calculator.

steps.title: Personal details
steps.asks: First name, last name and date of birth.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address. This country is also the country of residence. The canton is asked only if the country is Switzerland.

steps.title: Nationality and permit
steps.asks: The nationality. Anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss, even with another nationality. Non-Swiss employees are also asked whether they hold a C permit (yes/no).

steps.title: Civil status and spouse
steps.asks: The civil status, from the pension fund's list. The spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked only if the employee is married, in a registered partnership or separated. Spouse questions are asked only if the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, holds no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership. The first is the spouse's or partner's country of residence. If the spouse lives in Switzerland, the spouse's nationality is asked. If the spouse is not Swiss, the employee is asked whether the spouse holds a C permit.

steps.title: Source tax
steps.asks: The denomination. Employees who are married or in a registered partnership are asked whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income. Everyone in this step is asked whether they have children.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax: everyone living abroad, and employees living in Switzerland who are not Swiss, hold no C permit and are not exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse or partner living in Switzerland

steps.title: Children
steps.asks: One block per child, repeated for each child the employee adds. It asks whether the child is a minor or of age and in first education, and whether the child lives in the same household. Further questions follow only where the earlier answers make them relevant: custody, common household with the other parent, alternating care, who contributes more to the child's maintenance, and whether the employee mainly maintains a child of age (more than 50%).
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who have children

steps.title: Cross-border commuting
steps.asks: Employees living in Germany are asked whether they return home daily. With daily return, they are asked whether they have a certificate of residence ('not yet' is a valid answer). Without daily return, they are asked whether a daily return would be reasonable (less than 100 km). If it would be, they are asked whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days. Employees living in Liechtenstein are asked whether they return home daily. If not, they are asked whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who live in Germany or Liechtenstein

steps.title: Finish
steps.asks: Nothing new is asked. The employee submits the answers. Non-Swiss employees and all employees living abroad are reminded to bring their permit on the first working day.

flow.closing: When the employee submits, answers to questions that no longer apply are discarded. The questionnaire then becomes read-only for the employee, and any later change is made by HR. Lonio records for HR the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, and whether the employee is subject to source tax. It also records the source tax result: a tariff code, or for Liechtenstein residents the flagged 'in principle no source tax liability' result. All of these are always derived again from the latest answers.
